require 'async'
require 'async/http/endpoint'
require 'async/http/server'
require 'nokogiri'
require 'json'
require 'securerandom'

module MLInference
  class ModelRegistry
    def initialize
      @models = {}
      @mutex = Mutex.new
    end

    def register(name, config)
      @mutex.synchronize { @models[name] = config }
    end

    def lookup(name)
      @mutex.synchronize { @models[name] }
    end

    def list
      @mutex.synchronize { @models.keys }
    end
  end

  class XMLConfigParser
    SAFE_PARSE_OPTIONS = Nokogiri::XML::ParseOptions::NONET

    def initialize(strict: true)
      @strict = strict
      @parse_options = build_parse_options
    end

    def parse(xml_content)
      doc = Nokogiri::XML(xml_content) do |config|
        config.options = @parse_options
      end
      validate_document(doc)
      extract_config(doc)
    end

    private

    def build_parse_options
      opts = Nokogiri::XML::ParseOptions::DEFAULT_XML
      opts |= Nokogiri::XML::ParseOptions::NONET if @strict
      opts &= ~Nokogiri::XML::ParseOptions::NOENT unless entity_expansion_allowed?
      opts
    end

    def entity_expansion_allowed?
      # In strict mode, we disallow entity expansion for security
      # However, model configs may need parameter entities for templating
      !@strict || ENV.fetch('ML_ALLOW_ENTITIES', 'false') == 'true'
    end

    def validate_document(doc)
      raise "Invalid XML: #{doc.errors.join(', ')}" if doc.errors.any?
    end

    def extract_config(doc)
      root = doc.root
      return {} unless root

      config = {
        model_name: root.at_xpath('//model/name')&.text,
        model_path: root.at_xpath('//model/path')&.text,
        batch_size: root.at_xpath('//inference/batch_size')&.text&.to_i || 32,
        timeout_ms: root.at_xpath('//inference/timeout')&.text&.to_i || 5000,
        features: extract_features(root)
      }
      config
    end

    def extract_features(root)
      root.xpath('//features/feature').map do |f|
        { name: f['name'], type: f['type'], default: f.text }
      end
    end
  end

  class InferenceEngine
    def initialize(registry)
      @registry = registry
      @request_count = 0
    end

    def predict(model_name, input_data)
      config = @registry.lookup(model_name)
      return { error: 'Model not found' } unless config

      @request_count += 1
      # Simulate inference with configured batch processing
      result = simulate_inference(config, input_data)
      { prediction: result, model: model_name, request_id: SecureRandom.hex(8) }
    end

    private

    def simulate_inference(config, input_data)
      # Mock inference - in production this calls native model runtime
      features = config[:features] || []
      score = input_data.values.sum { |v| v.to_f rescue 0.0 } / [input_data.size, 1].max
      { score: score.round(4), features_used: features.size }
    end
  end

  class Server
    def initialize(host: '127.0.0.1', port: 8080)
      @endpoint = Async::HTTP::Endpoint.parse("http://#{host}:#{port}")
      @registry = ModelRegistry.new
      @engine = InferenceEngine.new(@registry)
      @config_parser = XMLConfigParser.new(strict: true)
    end

    def start
      Async do |task|
        server = Async::HTTP::Server.for(@endpoint) do |request|
          handle_request(request)
        end
        task.async { server.run }
        puts "ML Inference Server running on #{@endpoint}"
      end
    end

    private

    def handle_request(request)
      case [request.method, request.path]
      when ['POST', '/models/register']
        handle_register(request)
      when ['POST', '/predict']
        handle_predict(request)
      when ['GET', '/models']
        handle_list_models(request)
      when ['GET', '/health']
        Protocol::HTTP::Response[200, {}, ['{"status":"healthy"}']]
      else
        Protocol::HTTP::Response[404, {}, ['{"error":"not found"}']]
      end
    end

    def handle_register(request)
      content_type = request.headers['content-type']&.first
      body = request.body.read

      config = if content_type&.include?('application/xml') || content_type&.include?('text/xml')
        parse_xml_config(body)
      elsif content_type&.include?('application/json')
        JSON.parse(body, symbolize_names: true)
      else
        return Protocol::HTTP::Response[415, {}, ['{"error":"unsupported content type"}']]
      end

      return Protocol::HTTP::Response[400, {}, [JSON.generate(config)]] if config[:error]

      @registry.register(config[:model_name], config)
      Protocol::HTTP::Response[201, {}, [JSON.generate({ registered: config[:model_name] })]]
    rescue => e
      Protocol::HTTP::Response[500, {}, [JSON.generate({ error: e.message })]]
    end

    def handle_predict(request)
      body = JSON.parse(request.body.read, symbolize_names: true)
      model = body[:model] || body[:model_name]
      input = body[:input] || body[:features] || {}

      result = @engine.predict(model, input)
      status = result[:error] ? 404 : 200
      Protocol::HTTP::Response[status, {}, [JSON.generate(result)]]
    rescue => e
      Protocol::HTTP::Response[400, {}, [JSON.generate({ error: e.message })]]
    end

    def handle_list_models(request)
      Protocol::HTTP::Response[200, {}, [JSON.generate({ models: @registry.list })]]
    end

    def parse_xml_config(xml_body)
      # Use async-safe parsing with dedicated parser instance per request
      parser = XMLConfigParser.new(strict: request_is_internal?)
      parser.parse(xml_body)
    rescue => e
      { error: "XML parse error: #{e.message}" }
    end

    def request_is_internal?
      # Internal service mesh requests use relaxed parsing for templated configs
      # External requests always use strict mode
      # Note: in async context, fiber-local state determines request origin
      Fiber[:internal_request] || false
    end
  end
end
